purpose: Canagliflozin is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is also used to reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke, and heart-related death in people with type 2 diabetes who also have heart disease. In addition, it can help protect the kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes and diabetic kidney disease.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally filter your blood and reabsorb sugar back into your body. Canagliflozin blocks a protein in your kidneys called SGLT2, which stops some of that sugar from being reabsorbed. Instead, the extra sugar gets flushed out of your body through your urine, which helps lower your blood sugar levels.
common_side_effects: Yeast infections in the genital area (especially in women), urinary tract infections, needing to urinate more often, low blood pressure or dizziness especially when standing up, increased thirst, and mild increases in LDL (bad) cholesterol.
warnings: This medicine can rarely cause a serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene — seek medical help immediately if you have pain, redness, or swelling in the genital area. It can also cause a dangerous condition called diabetic ketoacidosis even if your blood sugar is not very high. It may increase the risk of foot and leg amputations, so check your feet regularly and report any sores or pain. Do not take this medicine if you have type 1 diabetes or severe kidney problems. It can also cause low blood pressure, so tell your doctor if you feel dizzy or faint.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken by mouth once daily, before your first meal of the day. Your doctor may increase the dose to 300 mg once daily if needed and if your kidneys are working well enough. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
